text:
emily: Heads-up 1: review of bulk revoke UX & warning hierarchy. Wanted to validate flow before design final.
rachel: thanks. main concern: bulk revoke can break many services. we should show an impact preview (dry run) and require a clear confirmation.
tom: impact preview idea: list affected keys + last-used timestamp + associated services (best-effort). show counts per service. keep preview collapsible.
juan: question: do we disable bulk revoke for org-admin-only or allow team owners? policy-wise we should gate by role. will need backend flag.
olga: a11y note: the preview list must be navigable with arrow keys and announced with aria-live="polite" when expanded. If it's long, provide a compressed summary first ("20 keys affecting 6 services").
emily: copy for the initial modal (draft): "Revoke X keys? This will immediately invalidate keys and may cause interruption to services. Preview affected services below. This action can be undone for 30s." thoughts?
rachel: language: "may cause interruption" too vague. propose: "This will immediately invalidate keys. Some services may stop calling Redwood until they switch to a replacement key."
tom: for safety, we should offer two options in modal: "Preview impact" (default) and "Proceed" (danger). disable direct immediate revoke from table multi-select unless user clicks "Preview impact".
juan: operational ask: show last-seen IP and last request time for each key in the preview, it helps teams decide. backend can fetch this from audit logs but might be slow for many keys 10k. consider capped preview (first 200 keys) and a note.
olga: keyboard focus: when preview opens focus should go to the summary heading, not the revoke button. If user uses keyboard to proceed, require explicit checkbox "I understand this will invalidate X keys" before enabling confirm. That helps screen reader users too.
emily: UX microcopy for the checkbox: "I understand these keys will stop working immediately and I have a plan to replace them."
rachel: also add a low-contrast helper line: "Tip: use service-scoped keys to limit blast radius."
tom: infra-bot: scheduled job: bulk-revoke-preview-cache-warmup -> staging (sha: c2a9f0).
infra-bot: job started: warm caching of audit indices for preview queries.
emily: action items: 1) design prototype for preview list with collapse/expand per service, 2) add checkbox confirmation and undo snackbar design, 3) role gating copy and granularity controls (filter by scope).
uan??: (typo)
juan: also propose a CLI helper for mass rotation rather than revoke. sample:

```bash
# rotate keys for service-worker bundle
redwood keys rotate --filter "scope:service-worker" --create-replacement --dry-run
```

rachel: perf note: make dry-run a fast path (cached result) else UX will be sluggish. show a spinner and an ETA if backend comp is expected.
olga: color/accessibility: danger red for confirm button must pass AA; if there are stacked warnings (banner + modal) ensure color contrast combos still readable.
tom: small detail: table multiselect label should say "Select keys (X selected)" not just "Selected X" to help screen readers.
emily: regarding undo: we can soft-delete server-side for 30s. infra needs to know about potential security model concerns.
infra-bot: note: soft-delete window must be auditable; events will be written to audit log with revocation_state: "pending" then "revoked" or "restored".
emily: final copy suggestions for the confirm button states: default disabled text "Confirm revoke (check to enable)", enabled: "Revoke X keys now". Danger when clicked and show undo snackbar: "Revocation queued. 30s to undo."
rachel: UX alternative: instead of undo, provide a "simulate revoke" mode that marks keys "simulated revoked" and shows errors in logs for testers. Maybe overkill.
tom: another tiny flow: for keys created with expiration, show a "rotate recommended" badge in the table when expiry within 7 days. clicking that opens a one-click rotate panel.
juan: sample JSON for policy snippet to include in help docs: 

```json
{
  "policy_name": "service-limited",
  "rules": [
    {"scope": "models:infer", "actions": ["allow"]},
    {"scope": "admin:*", "actions": ["deny"]}
  ],
  "rotate_days": 90
}
```

olga: visual hint: for the empty state of the bulk revoke UI (when no keys match filter) show a subtle illustration and two CTAs: "Create scoped key" and "Adjust filters". Make sure these are reachable via keyboard.
emily: ok i'll update the Figma with these constraints. any last nits?
juan: ensure logs redact full key values when showing last-used entries. only show masked tokens like abc...xyz.
infra-bot: deploy note: bulk-revoke-soft-delete-api feature flag enabled for internal test orgs.
emily: great, i'll ship designs to the PR and mark blockers if infra needs more time. thanks everyone.
